=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:14404-14415 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The latch sweep treats public comment markers or headers as authoritative staged-support latch evidence without verifying the comment author's association.
  WHY: Any user can paste the marker onto an `ai:needs-human` issue, causing the poller to remove the human gate, add `ai:awaiting-approval`, and post `/approved`, resuming autonomous implementation.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:14374-14382 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: `release_staged_support_needs_human_latches` runs in consumer repositories because its guard checks only for the workspace-restore script instead of restricting execution to this repository.
  WHY: Consumer support checkouts contain the script, so the sweep scans and can release unrelated consumer `ai:needs-human` latches, widening both the API cost and spoofing surface.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:14426-14446 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: If label editing succeeds but posting `/approved` fails, the issue remains `ai:awaiting-approval` without the command comment needed to trigger implementation.
  WHY: The label edit and command post are not transactional or compensating, and no recovery path reliably targets this resulting state.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:14386 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `gh issue list ... || echo '[]'` hides persistent API, authentication, and permission failures as an empty latch list.
  WHY: Expired credentials, outages, or 403 responses silently prevent releases and provide no operator-visible diagnostic.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:14386 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `--limit 200` silently prevents the sweep from seeing `ai:needs-human` issues beyond the first 200.
  WHY: Repositories with more than 200 stalled human-gated issues leave later latches unreleased without logging that they were skipped.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:14386-14405 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The sweep fetches the full paginated comment history for every open `ai:needs-human` issue on every poll tick, including issues that cannot contain a staged-support latch.
  WHY: The per-issue API and materialization cost scales with all stalled human-gated issues rather than with staged-support latches, especially in consumer repositories.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17335-17403 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The auto-reset does not clear `security_pass_failed_engine_sha`, weakening the documented deduplication contract across distinct engine SHAs from the same engine family.
  WHY: A project can be re-fired once per newly recorded engine SHA within the `security_pass_auto_reset_engine_shas` window, opening repeated audit/fix-loop slots.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17350-17398 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: In the self-repository, resolving the support checkout from `${{ github.sha }}` makes the once-per-engine guard operate once per main commit rather than once per stable engine commit.
  WHY: Any merge to main, including documentation or test changes, can grant parked projects another full audit and fix-loop budget without a cumulative cap.

- changelog.d/binance-blessings-249-parked-projects-resume-without-humans.md:the filename itself | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The changelog fragment filename uses the cross-repository prefix `binance-blessings-249` instead of a numeric issue or PR prefix from this repository.
  WHY: This violates the documented filename convention and makes the fragment harder to locate while affecting filename sort order, although current assembly does not fail.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:14418-14446 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The poller posts `/approved` as an implicit implementation dispatch without a narrower kill switch or protection against coincidental marker text.
  WHY: An operator's parked issue can be auto-released and re-dispatched when its comments contain quoted marker text, and the deduplication relies on the same body-only match.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "the poller restores `ai:awaiting-approval` and posts `/approved` with a `<!-- ai:needs-human-auto-release reason=staged_support_rebase_conflict engine=<sha> -->` marker, at most once per issue per engine commit, and never while a release marker already follows the latest latch comment, so a latch that recurs on the same engine stays for a human."
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh — `release_staged_support_needs_human_latches` body, the `already_released` jq check.
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The `already_released` guard exists but uses `contains($marker)` against the entire comments array, which makes the "release marker already follows the latest latch comment" position check too permissive — a release marker anywhere in the comments array disables future auto-release even for a different engine or for a re-latch after release.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  WHY: Any GitHub user can paste the marker or staged-support failure header on an `ai:needs-human` issue, causing the sweep to release the latch and post `/approved`.
  severity=high | confidence=5
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 14426-14431
  Problem: If the label edit succeeds but the `/approved` comment post fails, the issue is left with `ai:awaiting-approval` and no command comment to trigger `implement.yml`.
  WHY: No recovery path targets this state.
  severity=high | confidence=4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 14386
  Problem: `gh issue list ... || echo '[]'` makes a persistent API or permission failure indistinguishable from zero latched issues.
  WHY: The sweep silently produces no releases with no diagnostic warning.
  severity=low | confidence=3
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 14386-14403
  Problem: The sweep fetches full paginated comment histories for every open `ai:needs-human` issue in every consumer repository on every 5-minute poll tick.
  WHY: The work scales with all stalled human-gated issues rather than staged-support latches.
  severity=low | confidence=4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 14378-14382
  Problem: `release_staged_support_needs_human_latches` runs in every consumer repository with no `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` guard.
  WHY: The staged support checkout makes the file-existence check true in consumers, allowing marker-based releases outside the declared repository scope.
  severity=high | confidence=5

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: release_staged_support_needs_human_latches body (≈14378–14446)
  Problem: The sweep accepts any comment body containing the latch marker or failure header as authoritative evidence, with no author check.
  WHY: Any user with comment access can cause the poller to remove the gate, add `ai:awaiting-approval`, and post `/approved`.
  severity=high | confidence=5
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: jq `already_released` check inside release_staged_support_needs_human_latches (≈14426–14440)
  Problem: The `already_released` guard matches release markers anywhere in the comments array without an author check or positional constraint.
  WHY: A quoted marker can disable future auto-release, including for a different engine or later re-latch.
  severity=high | confidence=4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: release_staged_support_needs_human_latches guard `[ ! -f scripts/implement_staged_support_workspace.sh ] && [ ! -f .codex-workflow-src/scripts/implement_staged_support_workspace.sh ]` (≈14378–14386)
  Problem: The implementation checks for the support script but does not enforce the documented self-repository-only scope.
  WHY: Consumer checkouts stage the script, so consumer issues can be auto-released even though the handler never ran there.
  severity=high | confidence=4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: release_staged_support_needs_human_latches list call `gh_retry gh issue list --label "ai:needs-human" --json number,labels --limit 200 2>/dev/null || echo '[]'` (≈14386)
  Problem: The call silently caps the sweep at 200 issues and hides API or authentication failures.
  WHY: Latches beyond the cap are missed, while failures look identical to an empty result.
  severity=high | confidence=4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: engine-auto-reset block (≈17335–17403) and the jq `.security_pass_auto_reset_engine_shas = (...)` mutation
  Problem: Auto-reset never clears `security_pass_failed_engine_sha`.
  WHY: Distinct engine SHAs from the same engine family can reopen audit/fix-loop slots within the deduplication window.
  severity=low | confidence=3
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: release_staged_support_needs_human_latches — `comments_json` failure branch and label-edit success / comment-post failure branch (≈14403–14446)
  Problem: Comment-fetch failures and label-edit/comment-post partial success leave incomplete state without an operator-visible summary.
  WHY: A successful label edit without `/approved` leaves `ai:awaiting-approval` without the command event needed to dispatch implementation.
  severity=high | confidence=3
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: release_staged_support_needs_human_latches — per-issue `gh_retry gh api --paginate "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${issue_num}/comments?per_page=100" | jq -s 'add // []'` (≈14403–14405)
  Problem: Every candidate issue materialises its full paginated comment history on every tick.
  WHY: A repository with many stalled issues incurs one or more comments API calls per issue every five minutes.
  severity=high | confidence=4
- changelog.d/binance-blessings-249-parked-projects-resume-without-humans.md
  Line or code reference: filename only
  Problem: The fragment filename uses the cross-repo prefix `binance-blessings-249` instead of a numeric issue-or-PR prefix for this repository.
  WHY: The filename violates the documented convention and weakens ordering and downstream lookup contracts.
  severity=low | confidence=4
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: release_staged_support_needs_human_latches — label-edit + `release_body` post (≈14418–14446)
  Problem: Posting `/approved` is an implicit implement dispatch with no narrower kill switch.
  WHY: An issue can be auto-released when comments coincidentally contain the marker, and the dedup uses the same body-match.
  severity=high | confidence=4
